**SALES AI**

**Selling the pain**  
I sell relief from a specific pain. Not a vague pain like inefficiency  
A real business pain has a cost: Time , Cost, Risk or reputation.  
Regardless of what is being sold I need to name the pain.

Ex. Time cost: leads do not follow up fast enough. Admin workers lunch in productive hours. Staff wastes time chasing info. Processes are manual and repetitive.  
Money cost: Lost leads \= lost revenue. Slow response \= lost leads  
High labor costs from manual work(ex. Receptionist)  
Translation is that the business is leaking money.  
Risk costs: Compliance issues, data mess, inconsistent client handling, mistakes that lead to refunds, etc.  
Reputation costs: Slow responses make the business look bad. Broken or old websites \= loss of trust. Inconsistent follow ups annoys prospects.  
Translation \= people stop trusting the business

Gives us a PAIN with a visible CONSEQUENCE  
Each niche has different needs, pains and awareness cycles. We need to understand properly their pain.

**Filter:** If this pain continues for 90 days, what does it cost to them?  
If I cannot answer it plainly then it isn’t the pain.

**OUTCOME**  
Convert pain into a measurable outcome with a time frame

**Outcome** formula: In \[Timeframe\] we go from \[Before\] to \[After\] measured by \[Metric\]  
A metric is something the buyer understands and is quantifiable: ex.: Response times, Leads to call(%), Conversion rate(%), time to follow up, etc.  
Avoid things like : better efficiency, more automated (vague and vanity)

Measurable outcomes:

Timeframes:  
7 days fast setup  
14 days for a system build and tuning  
30 days for full rollout with measurable change

Before and after examples:  
Time saved: In 14 days we can reduce admin time or time spent answering the phone from 10 hours to 3 hours per week measured by team time tracking.  
Revenue increase: In 30 days we can increase the lead to call conversation from 8% to 15% measured by booked call per lead.  
Risk reduction: in 14 days we can standardize follow up so 100% of inbound leads can be contacted in less than 10min, measured by crm timestamps.  
Ex.2: in 14 Days we can reduce the average response time from 3min to 15s, measured by Tool. OR In 14 days we can reduce the amount of calls lost from 15% to 0%, tracked by our own system.  
Reputation protection(ex. Chatbots instead of humans):  IN 7 days you can cut down the avg response time on your website from 5 minutes to instant, measured by average response time

Gives the buyer something they can picture and makes pricing possible.  
You stop selling ai and begin selling a measurable business improvement with a deadline.

**THE MECHANISM**  
It is the How. The decision maker buys a simple process that sounds inevitable . Not the llm or the workflow or the tool chain.  
Formula: We do \[Simple process\] so that \[Outcome\] happens without \[Company pain\]/\[risk\]  
Ex. « We capture every inquiry, respond instantly, and follow up automatically until they book. »  That is a mechanism: repeatable, understandable and outcome linked.  
Categories:  
Capture, qualify, and route: « We capture leads, qualify them, then route them to the right person with the right context »  
If it is respond follow up and book (receptionist):  A mechanism will be « we respond fast, follow up automatically, and drive them to a booking»  
Collect organize and alert: « We collect info, organize it and alert the team only when needed. »   
Standardize, reduce errors, and prove compliance: « We standardize the process, reduce mistakes and create a real audit trade. »  
No tool names, no ai, ONLY what happens  
Sense check question: If I run this mechanism does the outcome naturally happen?  
If the answer is not obvious then it needs simplification.

**SURVIVAL:**  
Fastest way to destroy a good offer is by having a vague scope.  
A vague scope allows for endless requests, modifications and updates, moving goalposts and late panic.  
 We set boundaries before we take the money. Rule: if it is not written, it will be assumed.  
We define 4 things: What is Included, what is Excluded, what inputs the client must provide and the delivery timeline.  
What is Included: Exact list of what the client gets. Keep it short and concrete examples. (Ex.) one automated follow up workflow. One booking page and one intake form. One dashboard, one onboarding and handover session. Seven days of post launch tweaks. Avoid fuzzy worlds like « full automation system », « End to end ai system ». BE SPECIFIC  
What is Excluded: This is to stop scope creep, where we protect our time. Common exclusions: No website Redesign or No paid ads management. No crm migration. No content creation. No 24/7 support. No unlimited revisions. **RULE:** If it is not listed in included, it is not part of the scope.  
Client Inputs: To not stall, so that the project does not go late because the client is not providing something. We need to make it their responsibility. Ex. Of inputs: Access to company email, access to the phone provider account, Access to domain manager, access to crm, website, calendar. Maybe assets or offer details. Team contact when decision maker is not available, etc. **Rule:** Timeline starts when inputs are received.  
Delivery timeline: Give clear timeline with stages. Ex.: Day 0-2 Access and Setup, Day 3-7 build and internal tests, Day 8-10 client review and tweaks, Day 11-14 is client handover.  
This makes the offer feel real and avoids « When will this be ready » Every 2 days.

**PROOF OF PROXY**  
A decision maker will buy when they believe that It will work AND that I can deliver it.  
First need Belief of myself and then Proof.  
Proof stack: Hard proof:  numbers, results, metrics, screenshots, case studies , Soft proof : testimonials, referrals, reputation  Process proof : Delivery framework, scope boundaries, timeline, clarity(reduces perceived risk through professionality )  
Proof Proxy(no or low results to show):  Built prototypes(MAIN PROXY) for businesses(shows competence), they show what is possible to achieve and how it applies to them, without lying.  Pilot planned proof: Ex. We run a 14 day pilot, success measured by X metric (only really applicable to chatbot), if we do not hit baseline improvements we do not expand scope(belief through risk control). Transfer proof: We borrow credibility from adjacent proof. Similar niche works or related outcomes, previously built systems, or other things that demonstrate competence (ex. Own website). Logic proof: Ex. If response time drops from 12h to 10m, conversion rises because fewer leads are called. Ex2. If follow ups become consistent, no shows drop off significantly and bookings increase.  
Decision makers love logic and more when it is tied to business metrics.  
RULE: Proof is best, proxies are acceptable, lying is never allowed.

**PRICING**  
Set price BEFORE the negotiation.  
How to determine price: Operational reality. **RULE**: Calculate operating cost: Tools, time, attention, Delivery efforts . Not what it costs to make but what it costs to deliver clearly.  
**RULE:** Price floor \= Operating cost \*3 .  We **NEVER** go below that number because we lose authority.  
Step 3: Walkaway. We must be willing to walk away from a prospect if he is not able to meet the floor price. Disengage calmly.  
Step 4: Outcome escalation: Price increases when the outcome is heavier. They never decrease the price: Ex. Speed, faster results \= Higher price . Ex2. Higher scope \= higher price (touch more systems, reduce the buyer’s inputs or things to do). Ex. 3 Certainty: higher predictability increases price(proven processes, tighter controls, fewer variables). Buyers pay more to reduce uncertainty(ex. We say that we have done that system multiple times).  
**RULE:** Price only moves up when outcomes get heavier. Pricing never goes down because of the pressure.  
If they cannot meet that we walk away.  
What increases speed in my offer?: \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_  
What increases certainty in my offer?: \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_  
What increases risk in my offer?: \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_  
What increases scope in my offer?: \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_  
These are the **Price escalators .**  I do not negotiate them, I select them. I am not defending a number, I match a price to an outcome weight.  
When we have an established floor and exit, we stoop selling emotionally.   
3 Variables are : **Operating cost,  Pricing floor, walk away rule**

**THE OFFER**  
NOT « INSPIRATION »  
Offer is not what I do, an offer is a promise of an outcome.  
4 Components: Outcome, Mechanisms, Boundaries, Price,    
**Outcome:** « What is my life or business like after this works? »(For the client) This works only for the painful problem that we have chosen for the niche. If we widen it we lose clarity. **CHOOSE ONE PAIN**  
One outcome, for one buyer, solving one problem. Ex: We get agencies to contact inbound leads under 5 seconds. Ex2.: We get Local businesses to book calls without hiring staff.   If it needs a paragraph it is too complex (go back to outcome lesson).  
**Mechanisms**: Now the clients brain goes « Ok but how is this going to happen ?»  We say « We do this through\_\_\_ » Ex. We do this through an ai automated triage and response system. OR we do this through a pipeline engineered for retention.  We avoid mentioning tool too early as to avoid losing their interest. The buyer should feel this is a controllable variable. We explain our way of getting them from A to B, only explaining the spine of it. We say « In order to get you from A to B, We do X, Y, Z » Ex. In order to get you from lead submission to contact form in under 5 seconds, we install instant response, qualify intent and route the lead without human intervention. (3 steps MAX) **Subsection:** Unique **differentiator**: It is not I work hard, I do care etc. A differentiator is why ours work when other things fail (similar to agitate phase in PAS). We say: « This works because » Ex. This works because humans are slow and automation isn’t. Ex2. This works because it uses top ai models that are proven to precisely detect intent. Ex3. This works because most  systems respond late and not instantly.   We are not attacking competitors or their current staff, we are explaining the reality. The structure is : « Most people try to solve this by\_\_\_ We do it differently » Ex. « Most people try to use GPT prompts and basic automations and hope someone follows up, we install a triage response layer that eliminates that delay entirely. »   
We reassure the clients that it integrates with their existing systems without rebuilding or replacing their current systems. Fear drops when the things feel additive instead of replacing. Then we go to the scope \-\>  
**Boundaries:** We define what the system is, what it isn’t and how long it takes. Ex.: « This fixes inbound response speed, it does not rebuild your entire sales operation. Setup takes X days and runs continiously. » A clear scope prevents resentment or scope creep since that kills retention.  At this stage it is not a sales call, that has already happened, we are selling the execution. We say : « The **NEXT STEP** is » Ex. « The next step is we secure the investment and we begin implementation immediately. Once the investment is secured, setup begins and you will have this live within X days. After delivery we will do a walkthrough so your team knows exactly how this works»

Framework: (Outcome) We help buyer to go from \[Pain\] to an after without \[Pain\].  (Mechanism) We do that by \[Mechanism in plain English\] , (spine) In order to make that happen, we do X,Y,Z , (differentiator) this works because \[simple explanation why this fix is what keeps breaking elsewhere or what they have already failed at or what people have tried at and failed before\]  (Boundaries) You see this runs \[inside, on top of, or alongside\] your existing systems and processes. (Price anchor) So solutions like this typically start at \[price or range depending on the scope\].  
(Execution step) ex. We help agencies contact inbound leads in under 5 seconds without sacrificing quality for quantity, most people use get prompts and basic automations and hope someone follows up. We do this through an automated triage response system. In order to make this happen, we install instant response systems, qualify the intent immediately and route them without human delay. This works because humans are slow and most automation respond too late. This already runs inside your existing ghl setup and fixes inbound response speed. It does not rebuild your entire sales operation, and solutions like this usually start at 15000$ depending on scope. The next step is we secure the investment and begin execution. Once the investment is secured, setup begins and you will have this live within X days. After delivery we will do a walkthrough so your team knows exactly how this works.  
The offer should be structured like that.  
   
Compressed version(cold calls, gym conversations, unexpected settings, networking events): Must include the 4 main components. The goal is to get in the door. The structure is: We help to \[get outcome\], we do this through \[mechanism\]. It works because of \[differentiator\]. The next step is \[Next step\] .  
Ex. We help agencies contact inbound leads in under 5 seconds. We do this through an automated triage response system. It works because humans are slow and automations aren’t. Next step is a short call to see if this fits your setup.  
ex2. We help local businesses get booked calls without hiring staff. We do this through an automated qualification layer. And it works because we remove speed and follow up as a failure point. Next step is mapping this to your inbound flow.  
Ex3. We help creators grow consistently without guessing formats. We do this through a retention engineered content pipeline, and this works because we standardize what already performs. The next step is deciding if this fits in your content goals.  
They need to not feel rushed, and being inviting without pressure.

**SALES CALL:**  
This is how a call is structured:  
1\. Call control. : This is the opening frame. We control the first 60 seconds.  
2\. Diagnose first.  We find the real problem under the surface symptoms  
3\. Quantify: We put the problem into cost, time, money, risk, reputation.  
4\. Qualification : We confirm if that is a priority, if they are able to buy, if there is a timeline, if it is fit to them.  
5\. Decision map: We map who signs off, what approvals exist, what kills the deals internally.  
6\. Value frame: We summarize the problem, cost, outcome and the simple mechanism. Outcome first, no tool talk.  
7\. Challenge skill: (as needed throughout the conversation) Anytime they drift, we reframe calmly.  
8\. Objection prevention: (Also throughout the call) Surface constraints and decision criteria early as to not come to it later.  
9\. Objection handling: We need to clarify, isolate, reframe and confirm. No arguments.  
10\. Commitment engineering: I propose the next correct step and lock it into the calendar with ownership  
11\. Proposal discipline : Only if necessary, and never without a booked review slot.  
12\. Post call follow through: This recaps the advances decisions, numbers, next steps, dates and ownerships  
13\.  Exit rules: If it is weak, disqualify cleanly, protect time and keep the pipeline clean.

**CALL CONTROL:**  
**Ask for confirmation of time** :  «We still have 15 min right? » .  
**Structure(agenda)**: « Perfect, I am going to ask you some questions to understand your current setup and what is costing you. If there is a real fit, I will explain what I would recommend and what the next steps could be, if not I’ll tell you that quickly. Sounds fair?» This removes fear of a random pitch, establishes diagnostic/doctor frame, positions me as a selective energy, and pre-handles the « I do not want to be sold defence ».  
**Outcome of call:** Explain what success means. : « By the end of this call, we should know one of two things. Either there is a clear problem worth solving and we map out the next step, or we shake hands and we keep moving. Deal? » This relaxes the buyer.  
**Permission to lead:**  « Let me start with this: »   
**RULE:** If I haven’t diagnosed, I have not the right to propose.  
The goal of the opening is to collect micro yes’s.

**DIAGNOSE FIRST:**  
 They usually begin by telling the symptoms, we need to uncover the real problem/pain point.  
**RULE:** Diagnosis earns the right to propose.  
It will be run in 5 layers.  
1\. What is happening right now ? What made you take this call? What would you like to be different? This is done to get clarity.  
2\. Mechanism, or where it breaks. We ask: Walk me through what happens from start to finish. Where does it break most often? What parts feel messy or manual when it goes wrong? Why is usually the cause?   
3\. Impact, what it costs. How much does that cost you in a normal week? If nothing changes, what happens in the next 90 days? How does this affect revenue, time, risk or reputation? What is the hidden cost people do not see?  
4\. Attempts, what they have tried previously. What have you tried before? What have you tried so far? What worked a little and what didn’t? Why do you think it hasn’t been solved yet? What are you worried will happen if you try again?  
5\. Priority. Why now and what matters? Why is this important to fix now? Where does this sit compared to your other priorities? What happens if we do nothing? What would make this a clear win for you (in the next 30 days)?  
2 Golden Questions: Tell me more about that. What is the real reason?(with variants like what is the real reason this is on your mind, What is the real block here, etc.)  
Then we summarize, so the client feels understood.  
The questions in this order flow naturally.  
**TASK:** We need to write or discovery flow as 8 to 10 questions in our own words while keeping the layers.

**QUANTIFY:**  
The decision makers move fast when their brain does the calculation: Doing nothing is more expensive than fixing it.  
The 4 levers are **Time**, **Money**, **Risk** and **Reputation**  
The goal is to find 1 lever that hurts more for the niche/business. We want to anchor the symptom. « You said X is happening, lets put a number on it»,  
Then we convert to a frequency: « How often does that happen(daily, weekly monthly ».  
Then we convert it to a type of magnitude:  « When it happens how big is it (Minutes, hours, dollars, lost deals, complaints)»   
Then we project it  « So over 30 days that is roughly \_\_ hours lost, Money lost, deals lost, etc. »  
Then we confirm : « Is that fair or am I missing something? » This line keeps collaborative and not confrontational  
Time example: How many hours a week does this eat? Who is doing it? What is that person supposed to be doing instead? \-\> (quantify): So you are saying 6h per week across 2 staff, that is 50h per month. Time is payroll and mixed execution.  
**Money example**: For $ leakages(missed opt): How many leads come in per week?  Roughly how many go cold because of this? What is an average client worth?   For **Hard spent**(cost): What does this cost in staff time or external spend? Are there any tools you are paying for that are not being used properly?  
**Risk Example:** What happens when this fails? Has it caused issues before? What is the worst case if this happens again? Does this touch compliance, refunds, disputes?    
**Reputation Example**(customer exp): How fast do you respond right now? Do you lose people before you even speak to them? Any negative reviews tied to this? What happens if a competitor responded in 5min, what happens?It is not branding it is conversion.  
Back of the napkin math with the client.  
Full example: If you get 40 leads a month and 20% go cold because response is slow., that is 8 leads. if one of your clients is worth 1K that is 8K lost per month in revenue. (Then we soften): Those are rough numbers, but is that accurate?(keeps collaborative) Its that it is costing you X every month.  
ANTI pitch **RULE:** Do not jump into the solution right after we quantify. We want to hold the frame so we ask: How urgent is this to fix? If we solve this in the next 30D, what would that unlock? Is this worth prioritizing? Then move forward.  
Write questions, 2 for each:

**QUALIFICATION**:  
Not every problem is worth fixing right now.  
« Let me ask you a few questions to make sure this is worth solving. If it is I will map the cleanest next step. If I isn’t I will tell you that too. »  
This gives Permission to qualify, positions me as selective and removes awkwardness  
A deal only exists if: \-We can solve the problem cleanly  \-If they care enough to move   \- they are the actual decision maker. (The 3 are needed)  
**Fit**(is it the right problem?): « Ok, is this the core issue or a symptom of something else? What happens if this stays unsolved for 90days? What would a win look like in the timeframe you cared about? »  
**Priority**(urgency/timeline): Where does this sit on your priority list? What else is competing for attention right now? Why is this important to fix now and not later? On a scale of 1 to 10 how urgent is this?  
**Ability to buy**: Is budget already allocated to solve this issue? Would you investigate in something like this? What is the normal approval path? If we decide to move forward, what could stop it internally? (not asking for bank balance but mapping for financial ability) When do you want this solved by?  
Then we summarize: « Ok based on what you said, this is a priority because the cost is roughly\_\_ and you want it improved by \_\_\_ , budget is \[allocated or needs approval\], Is that accurate?»  
**RULE**: If it is not a priority with the timeline it is NOT a deal.  
Write 6 qualification questions, 2 for each section.: \_\_\_\_

**DECISION MAPS:**  
A lot of deals die after the call because we didn’t map out correctly who was behind the business decisions.  
Most internal buying is « can we justify this SAFELY ?»  We need to remove internal friction  
I need to ask to control the timeline: « Half me through how you make decisions like this »(then I shut up)  
I build a mental map of who controls. It is divided in 4 boxes:  
  \- Economic buyer: Who controls the budget. I ask « When this gets approved, whose name is on the spend? Who signs off? Who has authority on this? » If they hesitate, I found a gap, which I need to map.

* Influencers: Who can block or bless. I ask « Who else would weigh in on this? Who would have concerns? If someone internals says no, who is that usually? »  
* Process steps: budget, legal or operations. I ask « What is the normal prices for approving something like this? Does this require budget approval, legal or up sign off? What is the timeline you usually follow? What would need to be true for you to green light this quickly?» Goal is to convert internal talks Into real pathways with steps.  
* Deal killers: Who usually stops it. I say « What usually stops things like this from going ahead? What made you say no to something similar before? If we do not move forward, will there be a reason? » Surfaces past bad experiences, fear of change and hidden objections , Budget constraints and internal politics they may have.  
  What usually kills a deal is not talking to the actual decision maker, the person who cannot approve spend (messenger trap). 

I need those 4 points to map. We can map this clearly if not speaking to Decision maker: « If this makes sense, what is the fastest path to get this in front of the person who approves it? »  
Before ending any decision maker conversation, lock the map: Say :  « Just so I am aligned, you are the final signer, ops will weigh in, and finance needs to confirm budget. Our next step is we make X and make our next decision by Y. Is That accurate? » This confirms truth and prevent surprises later on.  
**VALUE FRAME** :  
**RULE**: Frame value until the solution feels inevitable, then and only then add details.  
Outcome first, mechanism second, tool talk last IF EVER.  
When they have technical detail they think subconsciously complexity. More moving parts more risk and headaches.  
**Current cost**(what they are bleeding):  
**Outcome** in measurable time bound way  
**Leverage**(Why this works without adding workload):  
Script after diagnosis and quantification: « based on what you told me the problem is \_\_\_, the cost is roughly \[time/money/risk/reputation\] , the outcome we want is \[measurable result in timeframe\].  The way we get it is simple, we \[plain-english mechanism\] so that this stops happening without adding headcount/workload. »  
Use outcome words like: Eliminate, Reduce, Remove, protect, increase standardize, capture, convert.  
All value framing should be directed in one(or 2\) of the lanes (time saved/money increased/risk decreased/reputation protected)  
We need the buyer thinking « yeah we need that »  
We can use this kind of line : « if nothing changes it you keep paying the cost every month, the fix is simply removing the bottleneck. Simply cause and effect.  
**RULE**: No tool names\! No engineering Lecture(unless they specifically ask).  
If they ask we answer in Layers. Layer1 « at a high level, it’s a simple workflow, we capture respond, follow up and book, then it stops. »  
Layer2(if they want more: « we plug into what you already use and set rules so it behaves consistently »  
Layer 3(if they really push: « We connect your crm so actions happen automatically based on triggers »  
To **continue** the value framing: « If we could deliver \[outcome\] in \[timeframe\] and remove \[cost\], would you want to see the next clean step? »  
Write the value frame in 4 lines : **Problem (**root cause), a **cost** associated to a \[time/money/risk/reputation\] , **outcome** (measurable and time bound) , **mechanism** in plain English. That is the value frame(essentially Agitate phase).

**CHALLENGE SKILL**:  
Authority without aggression. Respect comes from tell the truth over tension.  
Run the sequence:  
 1\. Anchor the relationship « I see. Good question. I hear you.  » (validate emotional content but not the content)

1. Permission to be direct: « Can I be direct?  I want to challenge you on that because it affects the result.»  
2. Introduce logic: « the reason why I say this is because what typically happens here is,… the real issue here is X not Y… »  
3. Offer a better path : « The clean way to do this is… Here is what I recommend instead. »

Types of challenges.  
(False problem)Client says: « We need more leads. » (I challenge): « Maybe, but leads aren’t usually the problem, they are the visible symptom. Before we chase volume I would like to see where the leads are leaking, otherwise you will pay twice. zThis is how you will prevent building the wrong thing. »  
(Speed/price)Client says: « we just want something that is quick and cheap » (I challenge) If quick and cheap is the priority, you will get quick and cheap outcomes.  The question is , do you want a system that looks good or that produces results? (Here we offer path)We can do a contained pilot fast, but we do not cut the corners that protect the outcome.  
(Tool obsession) Client says: « Are you using chatgpt or claude?» (I challenge) Tool choice doesn’t matter to the result outcome do, if we hit the outcome the tool is invisible, if we miss the outcome, the tool names won’t save you. (Redirect/offer path)Lets define the outcomes and constraints first, then we pick the simplest mechanism.   
(Scope creep) Client says: « Can you also add X, Y and Z ?» I challenge: « We can but it is a scope change. If we expand scope, timeline and cost can change too. The clean way of doing this is we deliver the core outcome first, and then we expand. »  
(Think about it)Client says: « Let me think about it.» (I challenge) « Yeah, when someone tells me that usually they mean 1 of 3 things. The priority isn’t high, the path I have laid out isn’t clear, or there is a concern that hasn’t surfaced yet. So which one is it? »   
Challenge is slow voice, short sentences, direct language. No extra fluff or words.   
Lane 1 is permission and purpose which is « let me challenge you on that for a second because it impacts the result. »  
Lane 2 is Reframe which is « The real constraint isn’t X its Y »  
The prototype creates belief,  challenge protects that belief.  
Write down 5 challenge responses for each scenario.

**OBJECTION PREVENTION**  
Most objections are late information.  
Humans reject what feels unsafe. When the risk feels high or effort they will say no.  
Question 1 that kills the objections, to ask before moving forward: « If we were to move forward, what would you need to see or believe for it to be an obvious yes? » This forces the buyer to reveal what they value, fear, measure, what the team will care about.  
Question 2: What would block this internally? (Legal compliance, bad experiences, budget, etc.)  
We need to clarify and de-risk.  
Framework to resolve: Table it, clarify it, de-risk it, confirm resolution.  
Ex. Client says:  « Budget might be tight »: I say: « Ok, budget constraint. »(label) « Is it not allocated or can’t justify? »(Clarifying) « That is why the next step is small. We can run a diagnostic or pilot to create certainty before we roll anything out. »(De-risk) « If the pilot proves X is the budget still a blocker? »(Confirmation)  
Ex2. They say: «Legal might block it. » I say: « what exactly would legal be concerned about? Is it data handling, permissions, compliance? If e keep it within your existing stack and avoid sensitive data, does that remove the concern? » Now we have the concrete blocker.  
Tool objection: They say: « We already have Tool/ai»(either they do not use it properly, they don’t trust implementation, it doesn’t produce the outcome they need, they want to avoid change).  **We say**: « What outcomes does that tool deliver? » Tools do not survive retelling, outcomes do.  
We also add « Is there anything you are unsure about even though the outcome is attractive? »   
CLOSING WIHTOUT OBJECTIONS (transition)  
We say « Based on what you have said, if we can deliver \[outcome\] within \[timeframe\] whilst respecting \[constraint\], that gives you enough certainty to make a decision without risk. »  
TO memorize: 1\. « For this too be an obvious yes, what would you need to see? »

1. « What could stop this, even if it made sense? »  
2. « Is there anything that you are unsure about that would make you hesitate? »

**OBJECTION HANDLING**  
If it appears, it is either 1.They are missing info, 2\. They feel risk, 3\. They are testing my certainty . I need to control the logic.  
The Loop is : Clarify, Isolate, Reframe, and Confirm.  
**RULE:** Never answer an unclear objection. Clarify first  
Ex. I say: « When you say it is too expensive(or any other objection), do you mean A or B? » Determine if it is about budget, risk, timing or confidence.  
Isolate: Ex. « If we solve this, do we move forward? » Or « If we handle that, is there anything else stopping you? » « Assuming that is resolved, are you comfortable taking the next step? » Or « Is this the main blocker? »  
Reframe: ex. if price: « What is the cost of inaction? » ex. Time: « What is the time saved? » « Is there anything you pilot we can do? » ex. If tool: « What is the outcome gap (?) and the usage reality? » Do they actually use that tool? Because if they did, would they still have that problem?  
Confirm: Ex. « Does that address it? Fair? » If this doesn’t work we loop back to clarify because there is an issue we haven’t uncovered    
Common scripts: Client: « It is too expensive » We say: « Totally fair, is it expensive relative to budget or relative to perceived value?(clarify) » Then «If the value is Clear and the path is low risk, is budget still the blocker (isolate) »  « The real question is not the price, it is wether it is cheaper than the cost.(reframe) From what you said you are leaking roughly \_\_$, and that is why we can begin with a contained pilot. » « If we keep it contained and prove the outcome first Does this remove the price concern? (Confirm) »  
Ex.2 Client: « We do not have the time right now » We say « When you say time, do you mean your team is overloaded or you don’t want another project?(clarify) » « If this required minimal amount of time from your team, could we move forward?(isolate) » «  The post of this is to give you time back. That is why we scope it, so your input to the deliverables are light and our outcomes are measurable (reframe)» « If we keep the inputs to these 2 need to get the work done and we handle the rest, can we take the next step? »  
Ex. 3 Client: « We already have a tool for that » We say « Got it, so what outcome was the tool meant to deliver and is it still delivering that outcome today? (clarification)» « If it is not delivering that outcome, would you be open to a better path?(isolating) » « Tools do not matter if the outcome is missing that gap, that is what is costing you. We are not here to replace tools for fun, we are here to remove the bottleneck. (reframe)» « If we can prove the outcome without disrupting what you already use, can we continue forward? (confirm)»  
Ex.4 Client « I need to think about it » We say « Of course, when someone tells me this it is usually one of these things, Priority, risk or missing information, which one is it? (Clarify)»  « Ok, so if we solve that, are you comfortable moving forward?(isolate) » « Thinking is fine. I just do not want you to get stuck in a limbo. Let’s get the real concern on the table so you can decide cleanly. (Or: and have the problem still costing you tomorrow)(reframe) » « What would you need to see to make it an obvious yes or no? (confirm)»  
Ex. Client: Now is not a good time » We say: « Is that because of budget cycles, workload, or is it not a priority yet?(clarify) » « if timing was ideal, would you do it? (isolate)» « If that cost is happening monthly, then doesn’t delaying it have a price? The clean move is to run a small diagnostic now. So when that timing opens you are ready. (Reframe) »  « Would it make sense to map it out now, so you are not starting from 0 later? (confirm)»  
**RULE:** After reframing, we should stop and let the silence. Do not always go through the loop. Sometimes the best move is to disqualify. « N worries, it seems like this isn’t a priority right now, if anything changes hit me up and we can revisit. If you like, I could send a small summary so we can pickup later. »

**COMMITMENT ENGINEERING**  
We sell the next logical step that reduces risk and increases certainty.  
3 steps.  
**Audit/diagnostic**: Clarity step, we want to use it when the problem is real but messy. We make a map to get as the outcome: Here is exactly what is broken and here is how to fix it.  
**Pilot:** proof step.  We use this when they want results but they fear risk and we need a quick win. Outcome: we prove the outcome in a contained scope(ex. Only using the vocal system on a single weekend ).  
**Rollout**: When proof already exists, and we can see the urgency is high, and they just want to go ahead and get the operation going. Outcome: we install it across the business and maintain it. If they are uncertain we push them down the ladder to the previous steps.  
Example script:(after value framing) « Based on everything you have told me, the next clean step is \[Select the one that fits\].  » Ex. For pilot: « Based on everything you have told me, the next clean step is to pilot the chatbot system first, so not a full rollout, and we will do this to reduce risk and give you certainty. If it proves the outcome, then we will decide if we expand. Does that make sense?»  
We have to determine on the moment what is appropriate.  
We need to assign ownership explicitly. I deliver, build and send. They need to do the necessary introductions, access, approval, or give data that I need. If ownership is unclear the next step is not going to happen.  
Calendar close: 1\. Agreement confirmation: « Sounds like the next step is capturing the leads coming in on your website, agreed? »  
2\. Define what happens next(in 1 sentence): « In that pilot we will do X to produce Y in Z days. » 

1. Assign ownership: « On my side I will\_\_\_\_ and on your side I will need to\_\_\_\_\_ . »   
2. Put on calendar: « Lets book it while you are here, are you up front with you calendar? (We give 2 options)…. I can do Tuesday at 11am or Wednesday at 3pm, which one works? (Closed question) »     
3. Confirm commitment: «Perfect I will send the invite now, once that is booked I will send you a short recap so your team can get aligned » 

After the call we send a short recap email, with the problem, quantified cost, agreed next steps, bay date and time, what we owe and what they owe. Outcome first.  
2 common commitment killers  
1\. Client: « Send me something first »  I say: « Happy to, what I do not want is you reading a doc and it going nowhere. Let’s book a 15min slot now and I will send you a summary to confirm that. »

1. Client:  « I need approval from X »  I say: « makes sense, let’s go ahead and book a short call with them on it so I can answer their questions directly. Otherwise it becomes messy game of retelling » 

Operator sentence to memorize: The call is not complete until the next step is **booked**.  
Write down our 3 next steps offers in 1 sentence each. (Use format we do X so you get Y in Z Days)

**PROPOSAL DISCIPLINE**  
**RULE:** We do not send proposals to convince, but to confirm .  
Only send a proposal if one of these is true: 1\. If identified on call that multiple stakeholders need it, or procurement requires it, there’s some type of internal process. Maybe the scope needs to be written with clarity or they ask for it after alignment.  
If the call wasn’t aligned on the problem, quantified cost, outcome, timeline, decision path(all variables), Then the proposal is not viable.  
A proposal should be something like : The problem we have confirmed or the cost we quantified, the outcome we agreed, the path we chose, maybe the constraints we respected and the next step we booked.  
**GOLDEN RULE**: No proposal without a calendar/booked follow-up.  
Ex. If client asks(in this context I assume cold call) it I say « absolutely I will send it. Let’s book 15min now to review it so it doesn’t end up sitting on your inbox. » Then false dilemma on the date and time  
Tips: Always put the outcome as the title Ex. « Reduce lead response time by sub 5 minute in 14 days »  Or « stop missed follow ups and recover lost bookings »  
Always put diagnosis on one page  
**TOBECONTINUED**

**POST CALL FOLLOW UP**  
**RULE:** The recap is not gratitude it is control. It should make the next step inevitable  
What the recap should do its to keep the problem clear, the cost real, the outcome agreed, Some type of ownership and some type of next step scheduled.  
Recap structure:  
Subject line: outcome first ex. Recap plus next steps. Reduced follow ups. Booked Tuesday 11am  
Body: Decision context (1 sentence as to why they  took the call) , The real problem (diagnosis, no big paragraphs), Cost, quantified (risk, money, time, reputation) Include 1 number min, Desired outcome, usually time bound, so before and after and the timeframe, Constraint or decision criteria, what must be true for a yes, Next step this is locked, we tell them exactly what it is and what it produces. Ownership So us vs them, what we owe, what they owe. Calendar confirmation: date and time and who is attending.  
Pro moves: 1\. « Summary for anyone else involved:  we are addressing problem, currently cost in \[number\], With (ex.)a contained pilot audit to prove \[outcome\] before any rollout(this is an example).»  
2\. « I would like deadlines for input. Please X by Friday so we can hit the pilot timeline. » Creates motion without pressure.

**EXIT RULES**  
Sales is about selection, not convincing.  
Chasing weak prospects is expensive.  
Exit criteria:  
1\. No priority: they like the idea but it is not urgent  
2\. No timeline: Some day is not a deal  
3\. No ability to buy: NO authority, no budget path, no approval.  
4\. No respect for process: They won’t commit, book follow ups or provide inputs.  
5\. Price only mindset: They only compare on cost, not outcome  
6\. Misalignment: Just the wrong fit  
7\. High friction early: I fit is hard before money after money it will be harder.  
How to exit:  
1\. Clarify reality: « Just so important accurate, where does this sit on your priority list »  
2\. Offer the clean path: If it is a priority the next step is x and we will lock it in on the calendar »  
3\. Wont commit just disqualify: « Don’t worry, It looks like this isn’t live enough to act upon right now.   
4\. Leave the door open: « If that changes, reach out and we can pick it back up »

Example scripts :  
If not priority: « Totally fair, from what I am hearing it isn’t a priority right now. Id not like to take your time if it is not live. If it becomes urgent later, message me and we’ll reopen it. »  
If No timeline: « Makes sense, without a timeline it is hard to do this properly. Let’s pause it, when there is a date you would like to solve this by, feel free to give me a call and we can move forward. »  
No authority: « Got it, sounds like someone else would need to sign off. The clean next step is we get them on a short call. If that is not possible we should pause until it is.»  
Price only(quote shopping): « If you are choosing purely on the lowest price, I am not the best fit. We focus on outcome and control. I do not want to win deal if I cannot in on quality. »  
Ghosting or weak follow up: «  I am going to close this out for now so it doesn’t sit open. If you want to restart just reply with the time that works well and we will pick it up from there. »  
Never make it personal, use not now language.
